items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Proposition: for a local complete intersection map A -> B, the cotangent complex L_{B/A} is a perfect complex with tor amplitude in [-1, 0] (source lines 2958-2962). The proof chooses a polynomial presentation P = A[x_1,...,x_n] surjecting onto B with kernel J and uses the identification of the truncated cotangent complex with the two-term complex J/J^2 -> (+)B dx_i; since J/J^2 is finite projective the truncation is perfect with the stated tor amplitude, so it remains to show that the other cohomology groups vanish. That is deduced from the distinguished triangle for A -> P -> B: the left term is computed by the polynomial algebra lemma, and the right term L_{B/P} has cohomology concentrated in degrees -1 and 0 by the Koszul regularity lemma, whence the middle term also vanishes outside those degrees.
